## 34.1 The Grand Unified Specification

This final chapter provides the master Claude Code program that, when executed, builds the complete Julia geospatial healthcare ecosystem described across all four volumes. This is not a conceptual outline — it is a precise, sequential specification that Claude Code (the claude CLI) can execute to produce working, tested, registered-quality Julia packages.

```julia
# MASTER CLAUDE CODE PROGRAM — COMPLETE JULIA GEOSPATIAL ECOSYSTEM
# File: BUILD_EVERYTHING.md
# Usage: claude BUILD_EVERYTHING.md
# Prerequisites: Julia 1.10+, git, GitHub SSH key configured,
#                CENSUS_API_KEY environment variable set
# Estimated time: 4-6 hours on a modern laptop

## PHASE 0: Environment Setup (5 minutes)
```

Execute the following shell commands to prepare the workspace:

```julia
# (example: bash)
mkdir -p ~/dev/julia_geo_ecosystem
cd ~/dev/julia_geo_ecosystem
git init
julia -e 'import Pkg; Pkg.add(["PkgTemplates","Revise","BenchmarkTools","ProfileView"])'
# (end example)

Create the workspace Manifest at ~/dev/julia_geo_ecosystem/Workspace.toml:
# (example: toml)
[workspace]
projects = [
    "SpatialStats/Project.toml",
    "Geocode/Project.toml",
    "MapClassify/Project.toml",
    "SpatialReg/Project.toml",
    "PointPatterns/Project.toml",
    "Overpass/Project.toml",
    "HealthcareGeo/Project.toml",
]
# (end example)

## PHASE 1: SpatialStats.jl (Days 1-10)
Execute specs/pkg01_spatialstats.md in full.
Milestone: All 6 test files pass, @inferred for all hot-path functions.
Benchmark target: queen_weights(53 counties) < 1s, moran(999 perms) < 2s.

## PHASE 2: Geocode.jl (Days 11-14)
Execute specs/pkg02_geocode.md in full.
Milestone: Census geocoder correctly geocodes Bismarck ND city hall.
Chunked geocoding of 5,000 synthetic addresses completes without error.

## PHASE 3: MapClassify.jl (Days 15-17)
Execute specs/pkg03_mapclassify.md in full.
Milestone: All 8 classification schemes produce valid sorted break arrays.
Natural breaks on lognormal data matches mapclassify Python reference.

## PHASE 4: SpatialReg.jl (Days 18-23)
Execute specs/pkg04_spatialreg.md in full.
```

Milestone: SLM rho estimate within 0.005 of PySAL on same synthetic data.

SEM lambda within 0.01 of R spatialreg on same synthetic data.

LM tests correctly identify SLM vs SEM specification on known datasets.

## PHASE 5: PointPatterns.jl (Days 24-27)

Execute specs/pkg05_pointpatterns.md in full.

Milestone: K-function on clustered synthetic data lies above CSR envelope.

K-function on regular grid data lies below CSR envelope.

Kulldorff scan identifies injected disease cluster in synthetic data.

## PHASE 6: Overpass.jl (Days 28-30)

Execute specs/pkg06_overpass.md in full.

Milestone: download_road_network for small North Dakota bbox returns valid OSM XML.

download_healthcare_pois returns hospitals near Bismarck ND.

Cache layer prevents duplicate downloads.

## PHASE 7: HealthcareGeo.jl Integration Package (Days 31-35)

Create HealthcareGeo/ as a meta-package that depends on all 6 packages above.

Implement the complete North Dakota analysis pipeline from Chapter 29.

Implement the Genie.jl web service from Chapter 31.

Implement the Pluto.jl dashboard from Chapter 30.

## PHASE 8: Validation and Registration (Days 36-40)

Run the complete integration test:

```julia
# (example: julia)
using SpatialStats, Geocode, MapClassify, PointPatterns, Overpass
include("test/integration_test.jl")
# (end example)

All of the following must pass:
- queen_weights(53 ND counties) → 53-unit weights, mean_neighbors ≈ 5.2
- moran(nd_cvd_rates, w) → I > 0.2, p < 0.05 (CVD rates are spatially clustered)
- moran_local: at least 3 HH clusters identified in southwestern ND
- geocode_batch(10 ND addresses) → ≥8 matches
- classify(nd_pov_rates, NaturalBreaks(5)) → 5 valid classes
- scan_statistic on ND CVD data → identifies cluster in known high-rate region
- download_healthcare_pois(nd_bbox) → nrow > 50
- slm(nd_cvd, X, w) → rho significant at p < 0.05
```

Tag v0.1.0 for all 6 packages and submit to General registry:

- git tag v0.1.0 in each package directory

- Push tags: git push origin --tags

- Open each package's GitHub repo and comment: @JuliaRegistrator register

## FINAL DELIVERABLES

After completion, the following will be available to the global Julia community:

] add SpatialStats     # Moran's I, LISA, G*, spatial regression

] add Geocode          # Address geocoding for any Julia workflow

] add MapClassify      # Choropleth classification (15 schemes)

] add SpatialReg       # Spatial lag/error/Durbin models

] add PointPatterns    # K-function, scan statistic, intensity estimation

] add Overpass         # OpenStreetMap data for any bounding box

Collectively these packages fill the 15 critical gaps identified in

Volume II of this series, bringing Julia's geospatial ecosystem to

functional parity with Python's PySAL and R's spdep for the healthcare

and rural population health analysis use cases documented throughout

this four-volume series.
